title: Community of embryonic structure reveals community of descent

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Community of embryonic structure reveals community of descent

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because the embryo is the animal in a less modified state that partly reveals the structure of its progenitor, two groups that pass through the same or similar embryonic stages are descended from the same or similar parents, however different their adults; this is why embryonic characters are the most valuable for classification.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, community in embryonic structure reveals community of descent.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “EMBRYOLOGY, laws of, explained by variations not supervening at an early age, and being inherited at a corresponding age”. Scope: animal groups, e.g. cirripedes recognised as crustaceans by their larvae

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Independent genomic phylogenies make the central evidential relation testable. The stronger claim that embryos directly preserve progenitor structure and are the most valuable characters is only partly discriminated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify embryonic character similarity among animal groups and test whether it predicts independently inferred molecular common ancestry and improves classification relative to adult convergence-prone characters. Agreement supports embryonic structure as evidence of descent.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Developmental similarity may reflect constraint as well as ancestry.

Embryonic datasets are strongly biased toward model species.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.72
data existence: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Concordance between embryonic characters and molecular clades is a workable reading of embryonic structure revealing descent, and it can be checked wherever both exist. That intersection is a subset of animal groups, with barnacles and vertebrates far better documented than the rest. The molecular comparison avoids using the embryonic characters twice, but sparse matrices keep the test partial.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare trees or distance matrices built from embryonic characters with independent molecular trees, and compare both with trees built from adult characters. The claim is confirmed if groups that share embryonic stages are clades on the molecular tree more reliably than adult similarity would indicate, and refuted if embryonic similarity groups species that molecular data place far apart.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The most conserved developmental stage is often mid-embryogenesis rather than the earliest embryo, so 'the embryo' is not a single comparable object.

Using embryonic similarity both to classify a group and to prove its common descent is circular unless the tree is molecular.

Comparative embryology matrices exist for scattered groups, not for animal groups in general.
